thread.title: Injury Sends MN Twins Star Back to IL - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Injury Sends MN Twins Star Back to IL - NewsBreak

author: Ted Schwerzler
title: Injury Sends MN Twins Star Back to IL - NewsBreak
text:
By Ted Schwerzler ,
5 hours ago
The Minnesota Twins placed Byron Buxton on the injured list just before the All-Star break . It was especially unfortunate because he had just been named a starter for the first time in his career. The hope was that he would miss the minimum 10 days, but he needed a few extra days before returning.
Now, after being removed from Tuesday night’s game against the Kansas City Royals, that same hip issue has sent the star outfielder back to the injured list.
Byron Buxton hits injured list again for Minnesota Twins Over the course of his career, Buxton has dealt with a long list of injuries. Hip issues have cost him time on multiple occasions, and this latest one has refused to go away. He aggravated it before the All-Star break on a stolen-base attempt and then lasted only two plate appearances Tuesday before exiting. Now he’s back on the injured list with no clear timetable for his return.
The Twins officially placed him on the 10-day injured list with a right hip impingement and recalled utilityman Tristan Gray from Triple-A St. Paul.
Buxton’s previous IL stint began before the All-Star break, giving him additional time to recover while the league paused. Even with that built-in rest and a few extra days beyond the minimum, he landed back on the shelf after only seven games. The minimum stay is again 10 days, but it would make sense for Minnesota to be more cautious this time.
The reality is that he has still put together a great season, batting .263 with an .864 OPS and 25 home runs. However, he had reached 3.0 fWAR a few weeks ago and has since slipped to 2.6 after going 4-for-25 following his first IL stint. It was clear he hadn’t returned to form.
Gray is batting just .232 with a .604 OPS , while his -7 DRS ranks him among baseball’s worst defensive shortstops. Recalling him allows the Twins to push Ryan Kreidler into the outfield, but there were more natural options available.
MN Twins skip over Walker Jenkins… for now Maybe the Minnesota Twins believe this latest absence will be short. That optimism is difficult to understand after his previous stint failed to prevent another setback, though. If they simply wanted a temporary replacement, they could have recalled an outfielder like Kyler Fedko or Matt Wallner.
Fedko’s first taste of the majors was rough, as he went hitless in 16 at-bats spread across 16 games. However, that sample is far too small to make any meaningful determination.
If the Twins wanted to make a real splash, this was the time to promote Walker Jenkins. The consensus top-10 prospect is batting .271 with an .819 OPS at Triple-A and has continued to show strong plate discipline. Minnesota would like to see more power emerge, but the 21-year-old looks close to forcing his way onto the major league roster.
Realistically, Jenkins should be on the Opening Day roster next spring, and getting him acclimated before then would only help. There may be service-time considerations behind the decision, especially with labor uncertainty looming after the season, but talking about aggression and then promoting Gray is certainly a choice.
At this point, a call-up feels inevitable, and this was a logical opportunity to make it happen. If Buxton’s absence lingers and the Twins continue leaving their top prospect in St. Paul, the decision will become increasingly difficult to defend.
